note: Discovery leads for web-development workers. Every claim, markup example, accessibility statement, browser behavior claim, and security boundary must be independently verified against current primary standards or platform documentation.

tierA.useFor: HTML elements, document processing, forms, links, images, and platform semantics
practical browser-compatible explanations and executable HTML/CSS/JavaScript examples
accessibility principles, semantic HTML, forms, alternatives, and inclusive design

tierB.useFor: JavaScript language semantics where MDN needs primary-spec corroboration
defensive web-security concepts; teach recognition and mitigation only

cautions: Standards and browser behavior evolve. Cite the current WHATWG, MDN, W3C, or ECMAScript primary source and execute or inspect every code example before publication; do not claim universal support without a source.

Keep HTML structure, semantics, CSS presentation, JavaScript behavior, networking, accessibility, and security boundaries distinct. Prefer semantic native elements before ARIA; explain that ARIA supplements rather than repairs incorrect structure.
Security content is defense-only: explain safe practices such as input handling, HTTPS, authentication boundaries, and recognizing risks without providing exploit instructions or payloads.

Use accessible examples: meaningful headings, labels, alt-text guidance, keyboard-aware controls, and sufficient context for links. Never promise that a single attribute alone makes a page accessible.
Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys from the completed review JSON and avoid duplicate question-stem templates.
